rule: A named event is a state machine with an optional unix-time window and no timer. States: enabled (armed), disabled (blocked), off, on. Start and stop only move between armed/off and on. The window is checked lazily when something asks (IsEventStarted): an on-event past its end is stopped, an armed or off event past its start is started, then the on-state is returned. Generators gate on the flag (GeneratorTimeType Event: active while enabled and started) or on the in-game clock (Day, Night). A flip is staged: the first check that sees a change only sets a flag, and the next generator update applies the then-current value, so the world lags one update and a reversed flip still lands. NPC emotes can start, stop or query an event; the query picks a success or failure line. Generator updates run every RegenerationInterval seconds (value not read).

data_fields.name: event_state
data_fields.unit: enum: undef 0, enabled 1, disabled 2, off 3, on 4

data_fields.name: generator_time_type
data_fields.unit: enum: real_time, event, night, day, defined (not implemented)

data_fields.name: emote_query_branch
data_fields.unit: emote types 23 start, 24 stop, 51 query; categories 27 success, 28 failure

keep: One named flag gates both a spawn (generator) and an NPC dialogue branch (success or failure line).
Lazy window check when asked; no per-event timer.
One-update debounce on world-state flips so a flicker does not repop or despawn a camp.
Start and stop are emote-driven, so a designer can flip an event from a scripted NPC without code.
change: The donor announces nothing on a flip; add a banner from the server ledger row.
Make the debounce explicit and keyed by event id on the server, not a side effect of a heartbeat count.
Do not ship a Defined generator type as a TODO stub; implement or remove it.
Keep the flag as the only server-written state; zones and NPCs only read it.
look_test: On the existing phone build, flip one named event on and off and compare at 375 wide: (a) the world only changes (a camp appears; the NPC line changes when asked); (b) the same change plus a 2-second top banner. Dom judges whether a player not looking can tell the world changed. Then flip on and off inside one tick: the world must settle on the last state with no flicker.
